_readme: The single source of truth for Italian terminology in Shopperino.
One English term has exactly ONE Italian translation, everywhere, forever.
references/glossary.md is generated from this file: scripts/glossary.py --md
Fields per term:
en        the English term as it appears in the app or the data
it        the Italian translation to use, always, with no synonyms
stems     optional list: the Italian forms that count as 'this term was
used'. Italian inflects the HEAD of a phrase, not the tail --
'tiro salvezza' becomes 'tiri salvezza' -- so a stem chopped off
the end ('tiro salvezz') misses the plural entirely. Give the
part that does not move: ['salvezz'].
Default when absent: `it` with a final vowel dropped.
en_case   optional, default false. true = match the English term
case-sensitively. Needed wherever the English game term is also
an ordinary English word: a skill called Search, a size called
Fine, a save called Will.
en_match  optional regex, when a word boundary is not enough --
'turn undead' is not the noun 'turn'.
never     optional list of Italian words that are WRONG for this term.
Scoped to the term: 'Vantaggio' is only a failure where the
English said 'Benefit'. Catches the case a stem check cannot —
a plausible synonym sitting where the agreed word should be.
strict    optional, default false. true = a violation FAILS verification.
Reserve it for proper nouns and rules terms where a synonym is a
real bug: class names, schools, saves, abilities. Leave it soft
when the English word is common prose, or the checker cries wolf.
kind      grouping for the generated markdown.
note      why this one, when the obvious choice would be wrong.

keep_verbatim._note: Never translated, never reworded, never recomputed. Copy them across exactly.
keep_verbatim.dice: 1d4, 2d6, d%, 1d4 x 10 — dice notation is universal
keep_verbatim.modifiers: +2, -4, –2 — sign and number both, including the en dash the data uses
keep_verbatim.units: the NUMBER never changes. The unit word may become Italian (feet -> piedi, pounds -> libbre) but must keep the same system: '10 feet' -> '10 piedi', NEVER '3 metri'. units.js converts at render and reads both languages.
keep_verbatim.markup:
every HTML tag, attribute and href exactly as-is:

, , . Translate only the text between tags.
keep_verbatim.slugs: anything that looks like an id: Link, ref, id, slug, anchors after #

en_match narrowed by the data lane: some spells count text glyphs, not player characters ('no more than six characters', spells.json Arcane Mark #23), and Ghost Sound (#223) uses 'basic character' to mean a sound's basic nature. Front-loaded the exclusion lookbehinds (checking only the word immediately before 'character', not a trailing lookbehind re-scanning the whole matched phrase) after finding that style silently checks the wrong text window; this form was verified against both the count idiom and the new 'basic character' case.

A wizard's or sorcerer's familiar. Not the English adjective: 'dwarves are familiar with valuable items', 'a place familiar to you' (spells.json Clairaudience/Clairvoyance #69), 'locate creature' (spells.json #307): 'this spell locates a known or familiar creature', a table-row label like 'Familiar (you know the subject well)' (spells.json #357, Nightmare), 'a creature with which you are familiar and send' (spells.json #457, Sending), 'not very familiar'/'Very familiar'/'familiar location' (spells.json #549, Teleport).
Stays 'round' in Italian D&D. Never 'turno' — turn is a different thing. en_match excludes the shape adjective ('round as bullets'), a different word entirely.
A combat turn. Not turning undead -- 'turn or rebuke creatures' is 'scacciare o intimorire le creature'. Not 'turn back' -- spells.json #431 Repulsion: 'tries to turn back toward you'.

Not a shape dimension either: '750 ft. square', '150-foot square' (spells.json #355, Move Earth), '20-ft.-square structure' (spells.json #454, Secure Shelter, hyphenated form), 'cylindrical or square wind walls' (spells.json #598, Wind Wall).
A weapon's or creature's reach. Not the English verb: 'if you reach -10 hit points', 'fall upward and reach the top of the area' (spells.json #439 Reverse Gravity).
The magic item (Staff of Fire, etc). Not the English collective noun: 'a staff of near-transparent servants' (spells.json #316, Mage's Magnificent Mansion).
